subject: Computer Networking
title: 6G: What Comes Next
description: A quick, practical guide to 6G: What Comes Next.

hook.text: 5G is still rolling out, but researchers are already designing 6G. Expected arrival: around 2030.

buildup.text: 6G targets terabit speeds, microsecond latency, and seamless integration of sensing and communication.

discovery.text: Terahertz frequencies offer massive bandwidth but barely penetrate anything, requiring radical new antenna designs.

twist.text: 6G may embed AI directly into the network. The network itself would predict, adapt, and optimize in real time.

climax.text: Digital twins, holographic calls, and global IoT coordination are the ambitious targets driving 6G research.

punchline.text: 6G won't just be faster. It aims to be intelligent.

quiz.question: What frequency range is 6G expected to explore?

details.summary: 6G research targets terabit-per-second speeds, sub-millisecond latency, and AI-native network intelligence by the 2030s.
details.whyItMatters: 6G research shapes the future of wireless communication. Understanding its goals and challenges provides context for where mobile technology is heading in the next decade.
takeaways: 6G targets terabit speeds using terahertz frequency bands
AI-native architecture optimizes networks in real time
Satellite-terrestrial convergence aims for global seamless coverage

faq.question: When will 6G be available?
faq.answer: 6G standards are expected to be finalized around 2028 to 2030 with commercial deployments beginning in the early 2030s. Research is ongoing at universities, telecoms, and government labs worldwide. South Korea, China, Japan, and the EU have active 6G research programs with significant funding.

faq.question: What will 6G enable that 5G cannot?
faq.answer: 6G aims to enable holographic communication, digital twins of physical environments, immersive extended reality everywhere, and sub-centimeter precision sensing. Terahertz frequencies could provide imaging capabilities alongside communication.
